facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: On the filed numbers the credit is a lightly levered industrial that took on acquisition debt in the first quarter of 2026 and has been paying it down. Total debt at 2026-09-30 was 4,037 against 2,909 at 2025-12-31; cash fell from 1,495 to 497; net debt on the same debt measure therefore rose from 1,414 to 3,540. On trailing reported Adjusted EBITDA of 1,431 that is 2.82x gross and 2.47x net, down from a first-quarter peak of 3.59x and 3.33x and above the 2.57x and 1.25x at FY2025. Cash interest paid is covered 7.73x on a trailing basis. Liquidity at the quarter end is 1,493 (cash 497 plus 996 available under the 1,000 revolving facility, net of 4 of letters of credit), with no loans drawn on the revolver. The only financial maintenance covenant described is a maximum first lien net leverage ratio of 5.50x, reported at 0.84x, and the arithmetic of the filings reproduces that figure from term loans, cash and trailing Adjusted EBITDA. The weaknesses are perimeter and definition: trailing earnings contain the acquired business for only the 2026 quarters, so the leverage ratios overstate leverage against a full combined year and the interest cover may be flattered because only part of a year of the new interest cost is in the trailing cash figure; Adjusted EBITDA is a company and credit-agreement measure with material add-backs; the legal documents are not supplied; and purchase accounting is preliminary. Confidence is Medium overall and High for the reported balances.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The credit is a leading but cyclical industrial supplier that has become materially larger and more diversified through a debt-funded acquisition. The legacy Allison Transmission unit makes fully automatic transmissions for medium- and heavy-duty commercial vehicles and for medium and heavy tactical defense vehicles, sells mainly through long-term agreements with a concentrated group of OEMs, and earns margins far above the acquired Allison Off-Highway unit. The January 2026 acquisition of Dana Incorporated's off-highway business was paid for with new notes at ATI, a new secured term loan, a revolver draw and cash on hand, and added two reportable segments, a much larger global manufacturing footprint and a lower-margin, more cyclical earnings stream. For creditors, the mechanics that matter are: a high-margin core with long-term customer agreements and an aftermarket cushion; a customer base where the top five OEMs were over half of sales before the acquisition; a lower-margin acquired unit with preliminary purchase accounting and open integration costs; and secured acquisition debt that sits ahead of fixed-rate unsecured notes. The issuer is publicly held with no sponsor in the pack, and its documented behaviour since closing is to repay debt (revolver repaid, partial note redemption) while continuing dividends and buybacks, which is mixed rather than extraction-oriented. Legal capacity to change that behaviour cannot be judged because the debt documents are not supplied. This handoff also corrects the earlier handoffs on pro forma information, set out in the correction section below.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Transaction. On June 11, 2025 Allison entered into a stock purchase agreement with Dana Incorporated to acquire its off-highway business (S1 page:56). The acquisition closed on January 1, 2026. The final purchase price is 2,628 (S4 page:7), after a 34 reduction for net deficiency in cash, indebtedness and working capital against a preliminary closing payment (S4 page:7); the annual report gave approximately 2,732 as a preliminary figure (S1 page:118). The sources disagree on the price at different dates and the disagreement is logged below, not reconciled. The acquired business forms the whole Allison Off-Highway segment (S4 page:7). Preliminary purchase accounting allocates goodwill of 770, of which 132 to Allison Transmission and 638 to Allison Off-Highway, and identifiable intangibles of 875 (S4 page:7 and page:8); the fair values are subject to change up to one year from closing (S4 page:8). The company expects the acquisition to be accretive to net income and diluted earnings per share in 2026, a management expectation (S7 page:4).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Financing and use of proceeds. The price was paid with cash on hand, 500 of proceeds from 5.875% senior notes due December 2033 issued by ATI, 1,200 of an incremental term loan under the credit agreement, and 300 of borrowings on ATI's revolving credit facility (S4 page:6). Lenders had also committed to a 364-day senior unsecured bridge facility of up to 2,000; it was reduced to 500 by December 31, 2025, was never drawn and was terminated at closing (S4 page:6). The notes were issued in November 2025 as a private placement and the proceeds were designated for the acquisition (S1 page:104). Debt raised for the acquisition is therefore 2,000 on the printed components (calculation A1), against a net cash outlay for the acquisition of 2,563 in the first quarter, reduced to 2,529 for the nine months after the price adjustment (S5 page:8, S4 page:3). Cash on hand covered the balance, and cash fell from 1,495 at 2025-12-31 to 311 at 2026-03-31 (financial base handoff).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: New debt issues and amendments. (1) 5.875% senior notes due December 2033, 500, issued November 2025 by ATI, unsecured; redeemable before December 1, 2028 at par plus an applicable premium (S4 page:23). (2) Amendment No. 5 to the credit agreement, entered January 2026 (dated January 2, 2026 in the annual report), added an incremental term loan of 1,200 maturing January 2, 2033 with a springing maturity to the term loan date if that is earlier, raised revolver commitments from 750 to 1,000 and extended the revolver maturity from March 2029 to January 2031 (S4 page:20, S1 page:119). The incremental term loan pays Term SOFR plus 1.75%, an all-in 5.54% at 2026-09-30 (S4 page:20). (3) Amendment No. 6, June 2026, lowered the margin on the original term loan by 0.25% (S4 page:20). (4) 300 was drawn on the revolver at closing, 150 was repaid in the first quarter and the remaining 150 in the second quarter (S5 page:1, S6 page:1). Deferred financing fees recorded on the amendment were 3 on the revolver increase and 12 on the incremental term loan (S4 page:20). Secured debt after the transaction is the two term loans, 1,699, against 2,300 of unsecured notes; the revolver is undrawn (financial base handoff). Liquidity effect: liquidity at 2026-09-30 is 1,493 on the financial base handoff, compared with 2,240 at 2025-12-31.

facts.label: Pro forma information and corrections to earlier handoffs
facts.text: The source-readiness handoff stated that a search of all seven sources found no pro forma disclosure, and the financial base handoff stated that no filing gave results of the acquired business for 2025. Both statements are wrong in part. Each quarterly report has a note headed Supplemental Pro-Forma Information (unaudited) that gives net sales and net income as if the acquisition had occurred on January 1, 2025 (S2 page:9, S3 page:9, S4 page:9). The search that missed it matched the unhyphenated spelling only. What is supplied: pro forma net sales and net income for the first, second and third quarters of 2025, and the nine months; what is still not supplied: pro forma Adjusted EBITDA, pro forma interest, any fourth quarter 2025 or full-year 2025 pro forma figure, and balance sheet data of the acquired business. Consequences: pre-acquisition net sales of the acquired business for 2025 can be derived by subtracting reported net sales from pro forma net sales (calculation A2), and its sales trend can be read; a pro forma trailing Adjusted EBITDA, and therefore pro forma leverage and cover, remain Not calculable, so the financial base handoff's leverage conclusion (trailing, mixed perimeter, overstated against a combined year) stands. Net debt over trailing EBITDA from that handoff is unchanged.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Allison Transmission Holdings is a solid mid-leverage industrial credit that is still working off acquisition debt. Its strongest support is a high-margin transmission franchise with long-term customer agreements, liquidity of USD 1,493 million with the revolver undrawn, and a first lien leverage ratio of 0.84x against a 5.50x limit. Its weakest point is leverage: total debt of USD 4,037 million is 2.82x trailing Adjusted EBITDA, a figure that mixes periods with and without the lower-margin off-highway business and cannot be restated on a combined basis. The outcome will be decided by how quickly operating cash flow retires debt while dividends and buybacks continue, by how the acquired business performs through a downturn, and by what the unseen credit agreement permits.
facts.basis: Literal wrapped paragraph from the model-authored handoff; no new analysis.

facts.label: Contrary evidence
facts.text: The strongest evidence against the synthesis view of a moderate and improving credit is the perimeter mismatch: trailing Adjusted EBITDA holds the acquired unit for three of four quarters, so reported leverage is overstated, yet the acquired unit earns a 12.7% Adjusted EBITDA margin against 37.8% for the legacy unit, so a full year would add less earnings than its sales share suggests (S7 page:10). A second counterpoint is that management's 2.0x net leverage target is below the 2.47x computed on the reported trailing basis, while distributions of 195 over nine months continue. Both would win if the pro forma earnings were weak or if the credit agreement allowed large distributions, which the pack cannot show.

### Readiness view

The effective source set supports the requested credit snapshot with limitations. All seven filed sources are retained: the annual report, the three quarterly reports and the three earnings releases, with every page of text extracted and no blocked preparation. The filings are the controlling authority; the releases are management attributions and are used only as supporting claims. The entity boundary resolves in the filings: Allison Transmission Holdings, Inc. is the registrant and consolidated reporter, and Allison Transmission, Inc. (ATI), its wholly-owned subsidiary, is the issuer of the senior notes and the borrower under the credit facility. Readiness for each consumer is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS. No consumer is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED, because no required source for the consumer's own method is missing. The binding limitations are: no executed legal documents (credit agreement, amendments, indentures); no pro forma or pre-acquisition financials for the acquired business; the annual figures predate the acquisition and use one segment; no maturity schedule by year after the January 2026 amendment; and an unresolved guarantor roster. These bound what downstream modules may conclude; they do not stop them from running.

### Financial base view

On the filed numbers the credit is a lightly levered industrial that took on acquisition debt in the first quarter of 2026 and has been paying it down. Total debt at 2026-09-30 was 4,037 against 2,909 at 2025-12-31; cash fell from 1,495 to 497; net debt on the same debt measure therefore rose from 1,414 to 3,540. On trailing reported Adjusted EBITDA of 1,431 that is 2.82x gross and 2.47x net, down from a first-quarter peak of 3.59x and 3.33x and above the 2.57x and 1.25x at FY2025. Cash interest paid is covered 7.73x on a trailing basis. Liquidity at the quarter end is 1,493 (cash 497 plus 996 available under the 1,000 revolving facility, net of 4 of letters of credit), with no loans drawn on the revolver. The only financial maintenance covenant described is a maximum first lien net leverage ratio of 5.50x, reported at 0.84x, and the arithmetic of the filings reproduces that figure from term loans, cash and trailing Adjusted EBITDA. The weaknesses are perimeter and definition: trailing earnings contain the acquired business for only the 2026 quarters, so the leverage ratios overstate leverage against a full combined year and the interest cover may be flattered because only part of a year of the new interest cost is in the trailing cash figure; Adjusted EBITDA is a company and credit-agreement measure with material add-backs; the legal documents are not supplied; and purchase accounting is preliminary. Confidence is Medium overall and High for the reported balances.

Trailing leverage on the plain reported measure is 2.82x gross and 2.47x net at the third quarter, falling from 3.59x and 3.33x at the first quarter. Direction check: after the first-quarter peak the gross ratio fell in each of the next two quarters (3.59x, 3.22x, 2.82x), and net debt fell from 3,984 to 3,741 to 3,540 (calculation C3). The trailing figure is a mixed perimeter. It adds FY2025 (no acquired business) to the 2026 quarters (with it), so it understates the earnings that the debt now supports. The acquired segment's Adjusted EBITDA is 285 for nine months and 83 for the third quarter (S7 page:10), and no filing in the pack gives its 2025 results, so a pro forma combined trailing EBITDA is Not calculable here.

The acquired segment earns a much lower margin than the legacy business: segment Adjusted EBITDA margin of 12.7% for the third quarter against 37.8% for Allison Transmission (S7 page:10). The consolidated Adjusted EBITDA margin has therefore fallen from 36.9% in the third quarter of 2025 to 26.1% (S4 page:41). This is a mix effect that leverage on a trailing basis cannot show.

Interest cover on cash paid is 7.73x trailing at the third quarter against 9.42x for FY2025. Interest expense, net for nine months is 166 against 67 (S4 page:2), driven by 49 on the incremental term loan, 22 on the 2033 notes and 17 of lower interest income (S4 page:38). The first quarter of 2026 is the first with the new debt, so the trailing cash figure holds three or fewer quarters of the new interest; cover on a run-rate basis would be lower than reported, but a run-rate is Not calculable from the filings without assuming a rate path for the floating loans.
### Liquidity

Liquidity at 2026-09-30 is 497 of cash plus 996 of undrawn revolver, a total of 1,493 (calculation C6), compared with 2,240 at 2025-12-31. Of the cash, 361 sits with foreign subsidiaries, mostly in Switzerland, China and India (S4 page:44); management says local restrictions are not expected to prevent funding of initiatives. The revolver of 1,000 carries a letters of credit allowance of up to 75 and 4 of letters of credit are outstanding (S4 page:21). No facility expires within twelve months of the cutoff. The nearest maturity is 300 of 4.75% notes due October 2027, which falls inside twelve months of the 2026-11-05 cutoff and about twelve months after the balance sheet date. Scheduled amortization is 4 per quarter in total. Management states that operating cash flow, cash and revolver capacity are sufficient for the next twelve months (S4 page:47); that is its assertion.

Uses of cash year to date (nine months 2026): business acquisition net of cash acquired 2,529, capital additions 149, dividends 72 and share repurchases 123 (S4 page:3). Remaining repurchase authorization is 1,068 (S4 page:47). Distributions to shareholders are therefore a discretionary use that can compete with debt reduction; the nine-month cash dividends and repurchases total 195 (calculation C8) against adjusted free cash flow of 662.
### Covenants

The credit facility requires a maximum first lien net leverage ratio of 5.50x when revolving loan commitments remain outstanding at a quarter end; the reported ratio is 0.84x at 2026-09-30 (S4 page:22). Reported ratios were 1.29x at 2026-03-31 (S2 page:18), 1.01x at 2026-06-30 (S3 page:20) and (0.87x) at 2025-12-31 (S1 page:103), where a negative value means cash exceeded first lien debt. Headroom against the maximum is 4.66x ratio points at the third quarter (calculation C9). A ratio at or below 4.00x also removes excess cash flow payments (S4 page:22).

Definition check: the reported ratio can be reproduced at all four dates as term loans and any drawn revolver, less all cash, over trailing Adjusted EBITDA as reported, without any pro forma adjustment for the acquisition (calculation C10). That is an inference from matching numbers; the credit agreement is not supplied, so the covenant definition itself is Not supplied. The ratio is a first lien measure and excludes the 2,300 of unsecured notes; it is not comparable with the total leverage figures above. Indenture covenants are negative covenants only, and the company states compliance with all covenants at 2026-09-30 (S4 page:22).
### Cash flow quality

Nine-month operating cash flow is 811 against 593 a year earlier, helped by higher gross profit and lower cash incentive compensation and reduced by higher cash interest and taxes and by working capital funding (S4 page:47). Operating cash flow includes 46 of payments for acquisition expenses against 30 a year earlier (S4 page:41). Working capital items in the cash flow statement are receivables (200) outflow, inventories 15 inflow, payables 207 inflow and other 12 inflow, a net inflow of 34 (calculation C11, S4 page:3). Cash taxes paid of 143 compare with income tax expense of 114 (S4 page:3 and page:2), and interest paid of 152 compares with interest expense, net of 166. Adjusted free cash flow is 662 for nine months against 492, and for the third quarter 278 against 184 (S4 page:41). Management guides full-year 2026 operating cash flow of 1,110 to 1,140 and adjusted free cash flow of 850 to 900 (S7 page:4); guidance is a forward-looking management statement and is not used in any ratio here.
### Adjusted EBITDA definition risk

Adjusted EBITDA of 1,166 for nine months is net income of 484 plus interest 166, depreciation 136, taxes 114, amortization 66 and a further 200 of adjustments (calculation C12, S4 page:41). Those adjustments are 64 of inventory step-up, 41 of depreciation on stepped-up assets, 30 of acquisition-related expenses, 25 of stock compensation, 17 of restructuring, 11 of unrealized loss on marketable securities, 3 of unrealized loss on foreign exchange, 2 of impairment and 7 of other items defined by the credit agreement. The adjustments equal 17.2% of the reported figure (calculation C12). The FY2025 bridge has 110 of other adjustments against 1,130 (S1 page:117). Acquisition-related expenses are cash costs that recur in 2026 and the footnote to operating cash flow shows 46 of cash payments for them in nine months (S4 page:41). The definition follows the credit agreement (S4 page:39) and the agreement is not in the pack, so the add-back baskets and any cap are Not supplied.

Litigation and consent-decree funding: Note Q states ordinary-course claims and says the company believes the ultimate liability, if any, will not be material (S4 page:27); no separate funding obligation is described. These are search results over the text, not a representation by the company.
### Latest quarter and events to the cutoff

During the third quarter of 2026 the company redeemed 100 of the 4.75% senior notes (S4 page:22), paid a quarterly dividend of 23 and repurchased 57 of stock (S7 page:1), recorded 17 of restructuring charges for off-highway footprint optimization (S4 page:41), and recorded acquisition-related expenses of 4. In the second quarter, Amendment No. 6 lowered the term loan margin by 0.25% (S4 page:20). Management raised its full-year 2026 guidance on 2026-11-02 to net sales of 5,975 to 6,075, adjusted EBITDA of 1,530 to 1,580 and adjusted free cash flow of 850 to 900 (S7 page:4); guidance is management's, not a filed fact. Purchase accounting is preliminary and was adjusted in the quarter with a 7 net increase to goodwill (S4 page:8). The latest dated content in the pack is the 10-Q signature date of 2026-11-04 (S4 page:54); a text search of the 10-Q found no subsequent events note, and nothing is dated after the 2026-11-05 cutoff.

Total debt is 4,037 in the debt note and 4,012 in management's release; this handoff uses 4,037 for every ratio and labels the other where it appears. The FY2025 annual statements have one segment; 2025 quarterly segments are recast in the 2026 quarterly reports (S4 page:29, page:30). The release debt and net debt figures were tied to the filings in the earlier handoff. Figures that depend on text extraction of flattened tables were read from the page text and tied to printed totals (calculations C3 and C12).

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Allison is a market-leading maker of commercial and defense transmissions that bought a lower-margin off-highway business on 2026-01-01 using 2,000 of new debt. It is publicly owned, has paid down debt since closing, and keeps returning cash to shareholders. | High | The sale agreement, credit agreement, indentures and the target leverage definition are not in the pack, so legal capacity and the pace of deleveraging rest on filing summaries. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| The legacy transmission business earns a much higher margin than the acquired off-highway business, which is now 42.6% of third quarter net sales. | Consolidated margins have fallen and group earnings now depend more on a lower-margin, cyclical business. | High |

| The acquisition was financed with 500 of new notes, a 1,200 term loan and a 300 revolver draw, plus cash; the revolver has since been repaid. | Acquisition debt is largely long-dated and secured or fixed, with the first maturity in 2027. | High |

| Management has a net leverage target of 2.0x but the pack does not define it, while dividends and buybacks continue. | Deleveraging pace is a management intention, not a covenant; shareholder returns compete with debt reduction. | Medium |

### Business and transaction view

The credit is a leading but cyclical industrial supplier that has become materially larger and more diversified through a debt-funded acquisition. The legacy Allison Transmission unit makes fully automatic transmissions for medium- and heavy-duty commercial vehicles and for medium and heavy tactical defense vehicles, sells mainly through long-term agreements with a concentrated group of OEMs, and earns margins far above the acquired Allison Off-Highway unit. The January 2026 acquisition of Dana Incorporated's off-highway business was paid for with new notes at ATI, a new secured term loan, a revolver draw and cash on hand, and added two reportable segments, a much larger global manufacturing footprint and a lower-margin, more cyclical earnings stream. For creditors, the mechanics that matter are: a high-margin core with long-term customer agreements and an aftermarket cushion; a customer base where the top five OEMs were over half of sales before the acquisition; a lower-margin acquired unit with preliminary purchase accounting and open integration costs; and secured acquisition debt that sits ahead of fixed-rate unsecured notes. The issuer is publicly held with no sponsor in the pack, and its documented behaviour since closing is to repay debt (revolver repaid, partial note redemption) while continuing dividends and buybacks, which is mixed rather than extraction-oriented. Legal capacity to change that behaviour cannot be judged because the debt documents are not supplied. This handoff also corrects the earlier handoffs on pro forma information, set out in the correction section below.

| Management leverage target | 2.0x net leverage; definition Not supplied | Management Language | S5 page:1: "2.0x net leverage target" |
### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Transaction. On June 11, 2025 Allison entered into a stock purchase agreement with Dana Incorporated to acquire its off-highway business (S1 page:56). The acquisition closed on January 1, 2026. The final purchase price is 2,628 (S4 page:7), after a 34 reduction for net deficiency in cash, indebtedness and working capital against a preliminary closing payment (S4 page:7); the annual report gave approximately 2,732 as a preliminary figure (S1 page:118). The sources disagree on the price at different dates and the disagreement is logged below, not reconciled. The acquired business forms the whole Allison Off-Highway segment (S4 page:7). Preliminary purchase accounting allocates goodwill of 770, of which 132 to Allison Transmission and 638 to Allison Off-Highway, and identifiable intangibles of 875 (S4 page:7 and page:8); the fair values are subject to change up to one year from closing (S4 page:8). The company expects the acquisition to be accretive to net income and diluted earnings per share in 2026, a management expectation (S7 page:4).

Financing and use of proceeds. The price was paid with cash on hand, 500 of proceeds from 5.875% senior notes due December 2033 issued by ATI, 1,200 of an incremental term loan under the credit agreement, and 300 of borrowings on ATI's revolving credit facility (S4 page:6). Lenders had also committed to a 364-day senior unsecured bridge facility of up to 2,000; it was reduced to 500 by December 31, 2025, was never drawn and was terminated at closing (S4 page:6). The notes were issued in November 2025 as a private placement and the proceeds were designated for the acquisition (S1 page:104). Debt raised for the acquisition is therefore 2,000 on the printed components (calculation A1), against a net cash outlay for the acquisition of 2,563 in the first quarter, reduced to 2,529 for the nine months after the price adjustment (S5 page:8, S4 page:3). Cash on hand covered the balance, and cash fell from 1,495 at 2025-12-31 to 311 at 2026-03-31 (financial base handoff).

New debt issues and amendments. (1) 5.875% senior notes due December 2033, 500, issued November 2025 by ATI, unsecured; redeemable before December 1, 2028 at par plus an applicable premium (S4 page:23). (2) Amendment No. 5 to the credit agreement, entered January 2026 (dated January 2, 2026 in the annual report), added an incremental term loan of 1,200 maturing January 2, 2033 with a springing maturity to the term loan date if that is earlier, raised revolver commitments from 750 to 1,000 and extended the revolver maturity from March 2029 to January 2031 (S4 page:20, S1 page:119). The incremental term loan pays Term SOFR plus 1.75%, an all-in 5.54% at 2026-09-30 (S4 page:20). (3) Amendment No. 6, June 2026, lowered the margin on the original term loan by 0.25% (S4 page:20). (4) 300 was drawn on the revolver at closing, 150 was repaid in the first quarter and the remaining 150 in the second quarter (S5 page:1, S6 page:1). Deferred financing fees recorded on the amendment were 3 on the revolver increase and 12 on the incremental term loan (S4 page:20). Secured debt after the transaction is the two term loans, 1,699, against 2,300 of unsecured notes; the revolver is undrawn (financial base handoff). Liquidity effect: liquidity at 2026-09-30 is 1,493 on the financial base handoff, compared with 2,240 at 2025-12-31.

Status and gaps. The transaction is completed; integration and purchase accounting are open. The sale agreement, the credit agreement and its amendments, the note indentures and the commitment letter are not in the pack (context records legal documents as none), so conditions, indemnities, purchase price adjustment mechanics and any earn-out or deferred consideration are Not supplied. The 2.0x net leverage target stated by management is not defined in the pack, and the financial base handoff computes net leverage of 2.47x on a trailing reported basis that mixes perimeters, so the two are not comparable and no gap to target is stated here.
### Pro forma information and corrections to earlier handoffs

The source-readiness handoff stated that a search of all seven sources found no pro forma disclosure, and the financial base handoff stated that no filing gave results of the acquired business for 2025. Both statements are wrong in part. Each quarterly report has a note headed Supplemental Pro-Forma Information (unaudited) that gives net sales and net income as if the acquisition had occurred on January 1, 2025 (S2 page:9, S3 page:9, S4 page:9). The search that missed it matched the unhyphenated spelling only. What is supplied: pro forma net sales and net income for the first, second and third quarters of 2025, and the nine months; what is still not supplied: pro forma Adjusted EBITDA, pro forma interest, any fourth quarter 2025 or full-year 2025 pro forma figure, and balance sheet data of the acquired business. Consequences: pre-acquisition net sales of the acquired business for 2025 can be derived by subtracting reported net sales from pro forma net sales (calculation A2), and its sales trend can be read; a pro forma trailing Adjusted EBITDA, and therefore pro forma leverage and cover, remain Not calculable, so the financial base handoff's leverage conclusion (trailing, mixed perimeter, overstated against a combined year) stands. Net debt over trailing EBITDA from that handoff is unchanged.

spans.text: ## Request

This is the fundamental credit synthesis for Allison Transmission Holdings Inc as of 2026-11-05, on the credit_snapshot pathway. Scope is business risk, financial risk, liquidity and the gaps that limit them, built only from the upstream handoffs, with no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.
## Sources

The synthesis uses the three upstream handoffs below. They rest on the seven issuer sources listed, which were not re-read for new facts here; every figure is taken from the handoffs and carries their period and perimeter labels.
### Issuer sources relied on through the handoffs

| S2 | 10-Q_2026-03-31_alsn-20260331.htm.jsonl | be0a328aec24e49cdf0300569cba1bccab7cce3c7f95d5658c5db76418cb7b3d |
Run settings, not issuer evidence: context file 1411207-allison-transmission-holdings-inc-alsn.json, sha256 f65312705cd8bb204fde9755509326ba975099b166b8d246c949fcd0ea955b5a.
### Supplied handoffs

| CP-0 | 944a1fdb32b0e105bdb98bcce7fe9920a9ab8a1870c238bf911cb1860242755e | source readiness |

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Allison is a solid mid-leverage industrial credit with a high-margin core, large liquidity and wide covenant headroom, but it still carries acquisition debt of USD 4,037 million and has not shown combined-business leverage. | Medium | Earnings before interest and depreciation cannot be put on a combined basis, and the credit agreement and indentures are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Trailing leverage peaked at 3.59x total after the acquisition and was 2.82x total and 2.47x net at 30 September 2026. | Leverage is falling but remains well above the 1.25x net level of year-end 2025. | Medium |

| Liquidity is USD 1,493 million, the first maturity is USD 300 million of notes in October 2027, and the only financial covenant sits at 0.84x against 5.50x. | Refinancing and covenant risk are low for the next two years. | High |

| At current rates, annual cash interest on funded debt is about USD 203 million, giving 7.04x cover on trailing Adjusted EBITDA against 7.73x on cash interest paid. | Interest burden is manageable, and the trailing figure slightly flatters coverage. | Medium |

| The acquired off-highway business has a 12.7% margin against 37.8% for the legacy business and is 42.6% of third quarter sales. | Group margin is lower and more cyclical than before the acquisition. | High |

| Dividends and repurchases of USD 195 million over nine months continue, while management's 2.0x net leverage target is undefined. | Debt reduction competes with shareholder returns and is not contractually committed. | Medium |
### Credit view

Allison Transmission Holdings is a solid mid-leverage industrial credit that is still working off acquisition debt. Its strongest support is a high-margin transmission franchise with long-term customer agreements, liquidity of USD 1,493 million with the revolver undrawn, and a first lien leverage ratio of 0.84x against a 5.50x limit. Its weakest point is leverage: total debt of USD 4,037 million is 2.82x trailing Adjusted EBITDA, a figure that mixes periods with and without the lower-margin off-highway business and cannot be restated on a combined basis. The outcome will be decided by how quickly operating cash flow retires debt while dividends and buybacks continue, by how the acquired business performs through a downturn, and by what the unseen credit agreement permits.
### Credit assessment
| Assessment | Category | Confidence | Basis | Limitation |

| Fundamental credit view: moderate credit risk, leverage elevated against the issuer's own history but covered by liquidity and strong cash generation; direction improving since the first quarter of 2026 | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Financial base: leverage, liquidity, covenant and cash flow sections; business and transaction: operating model, transaction and governance sections | Confidence is below High because combined-business earnings, legal documents and post-acquisition customer data are not supplied |
### Thesis

Allison combines a franchise with high margins and a long-term customer base with a large liquidity cushion, so acquisition leverage of 2.82x trailing is serviceable and falling, provided that the lower-margin acquired business holds its earnings and shareholder returns do not slow deleveraging.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strength, franchise margin (Documentary Fact). The legacy Allison Transmission unit earned an Adjusted EBITDA margin of 37.8% in the third quarter of 2026, well above the 12.7% of the acquired unit, so it carries most of group earnings.

Strength, revenue visibility (Documentary Fact). Long-term agreements with OEMs cover over 90% of North American on-highway unit volume and run three to five years; they set pricing and commodity cost sharing but not committed volume.
Strength, liquidity (Documentary Fact). Cash of USD 497 million and revolver availability of USD 996 million give USD 1,493 million, with nothing drawn on the revolver, which matures in January 2031.

Strength, covenant headroom (Documentary Fact). The single maintenance test, a maximum first lien net leverage ratio of 5.50x, was 0.84x at 30 September 2026; it is tested when revolving loan commitments remain outstanding and is reproduced from filed numbers.
Strength, cash generation and deleveraging (Documentary Fact). Adjusted free cash flow was USD 662 million for nine months 2026; the revolver was repaid and USD 100 million of notes redeemed.

Strength, debt structure (Documentary Fact). Maturities are spread: USD 300 million in 2027, USD 500 million in 2029, USD 1,505 million in 2031 and USD 1,694 million in 2033, with USD 2,300 million of fixed-rate notes.

Strength, end-market balance (Analyst Interpretation). Defense and aftermarket sales add counter-cyclical stability, and the acquisition added construction, agriculture, mining and industrial markets, though management describes industrial and agriculture demand as subdued.
Weakness, acquisition leverage (Documentary Fact). Net debt rose from USD 1,414 million at year-end 2025 to USD 3,540 million at 30 September 2026 on the note-total debt measure.

Weakness, perimeter mismatch (Insufficient Information). Trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,431 million holds the acquired unit for only three quarters; pro forma net sales and net income exist but pro forma Adjusted EBITDA does not, so combined leverage is Not calculable.

Weakness, lower-margin and cyclical acquired unit (Documentary Fact). The acquired unit is 42.6% of third quarter net sales with a 12.7% margin, its purchase accounting is preliminary, and integration costs continue.

Weakness, customer concentration (Documentary Fact). The top five OEM customers were 52% of FY2025 net sales before the acquisition, with Daimler AG at 18%; the post-acquisition split is not supplied.
Weakness, shareholder returns (Management Language). Dividends and repurchases of USD 195 million for nine months 2026 continue while management states a 2.0x net leverage target without defining it.

Weakness, earnings definition (Documentary Fact). Adjusted EBITDA includes USD 200 million of adjustments for nine months, 17.2% of the reported figure, defined by a credit agreement that is not supplied.

Weakness, structure and documentation (Insufficient Information). Secured term loans of USD 1,699 million rank ahead of USD 2,300 million of unsecured notes; the guarantor roster is unresolved and legal documents are not supplied.
### Key findings

First (Documentary Fact). Total debt to trailing Adjusted EBITDA peaked at 3.59x at the first quarter of 2026 and was 2.82x at the third quarter, against 2.57x at year-end 2025; net debt to trailing Adjusted EBITDA was 2.47x against 1.25x. Leverage has stepped up and is coming down, so the trajectory rather than the level supports the credit.

Second (Documentary Fact). Liquidity of USD 1,493 million covers the USD 300 million of 2027 notes about five times (calculation B2), and the revolver is undrawn. Refinancing risk is low through 2027, though the 2029 to 2033 maturities are larger.

Third (Analyst Interpretation). With 30 September 2026 rates held constant, annual cash interest on funded debt is about USD 203 million (calculation B1), and trailing Adjusted EBITDA covers it 7.04x, against 7.73x on trailing cash interest paid. The financial base said a run-rate could not be calculated without a rate path; holding quarter-end rates constant it can be estimated, and it is lower than the trailing figure.

Fourth (Analyst Interpretation). Earnings would have to fall about 85% before the first lien covenant ratio reached 5.50x (calculation B3). The covenant gives lenders little early warning and does not constrain distributions.

Fifth (Documentary Fact). Adjusted free cash flow of USD 662 million exceeded dividends and repurchases of USD 195 million by USD 467 million for nine months (calculation B4), which is about 13% of net debt. Retained cash is the main source of further debt reduction.

Sixth (Documentary Fact). Each quarterly report gives unaudited pro forma net sales and net income as if the acquisition had occurred on 2025-01-01, which corrects the earlier statements that none existed. Derived sales of the acquired unit grew 4.1% in the third quarter and 7.6% for nine months over the same periods of 2025, so the unit is not shrinking on a derived basis; its earnings before interest and depreciation are still unknown.

Seventh (Analyst Interpretation). The reported covenant ratio matches term loans less all cash over reported trailing Adjusted EBITDA, with no pro forma credit for the acquired unit's earlier quarters. The covenant measures reported earnings, so it does not capture a full year of the acquired unit's earnings.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Cyclical downturn in North American trucks or off-highway markets | Volumes fall in medium-duty and Class 8 vocational trucks, and in construction and agriculture; the acquired unit has lower margins and so less buffer | Adjusted EBITDA falls against fixed debt of USD 4,037 million; leverage rises from 2.82x; the first lien covenant would not bind but total leverage would | Material |

| Integration and purchase accounting of the acquired unit | Footprint restructuring, stepped-up inventory and preliminary fair values affect cash and reported earnings through 2026 | Cash costs and lower earnings delay deleveraging; goodwill and intangibles of USD 4,410 million are over half of assets (calculation B5) and exposed to impairment | Material |

| Distribution policy | Cash returned through dividends and buybacks competes with debt repayment; the 2.0x target is not defined or dated | The pace of deleveraging depends on management choice, not on a covenant | Material |
| Customer concentration | Top five OEMs were over half of FY2025 net sales; loss or model discontinuation cuts volume | Revenue and margin risk; the post-acquisition mix is Not supplied | Material |

| Earnings quality | Adjusted EBITDA adds back USD 200 million for nine months, defined by an unseen agreement | Leverage on adjusted earnings may understate leverage on plain accounting earnings | Material |

| Refinancing 2027 to 2033 | Notes of USD 300 million due October 2027, USD 500 million 2029, then USD 1,505 million in 2031 and USD 1,694 million in 2033 | Manageable with current liquidity and cash generation; larger maturities depend on market access | Minor |

| Floating-rate exposure | Term loans of USD 1,699 million float over Term SOFR; hedging of this exposure is not assessed in the handoffs | A one percentage point rise in rates adds about USD 17 million of annual cash interest (calculation B6) | Minor |

| Documentation and structure | Legal capacity under the credit agreement and indentures, and the guarantor roster, are unknown | Priming, restricted payment or collateral questions cannot be answered from the pack | Material |
### Corrections to upstream handoffs

Source readiness stated that a search of all sources found no pro forma disclosure, and the financial base stated that results of the acquired business for 2025 were not supplied and that a run-rate interest cover was not calculable. The business and transaction handoff corrected the first point: each quarterly report has supplemental pro forma net sales and net income. This handoff refines the second: holding 30 September 2026 rates constant, run-rate cash interest can be estimated (calculation B1), although it remains an estimate that excludes fees, hedges and interest income. Pro forma Adjusted EBITDA, pro forma interest and any fourth quarter 2025 pro forma figure remain Not supplied, so the conclusion that combined leverage is Not calculable stands.
## Calculations
All inputs are figures from the financial base handoff (FB) and the business and transaction handoff (BT), in US$ millions unless a ratio is stated.
| Id | Calculation | Inputs | Result |

| B1 | Run-rate annual cash interest on funded debt at 30 September 2026 | Notes: 300 x 4.75% = 14.25; 500 x 5.875% = 29.375; 1,000 x 3.75% = 37.5; 500 x 5.875% = 29.375. ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Every material figure in the credit work traces to a filed page and recomputes, apart from one rounding slip and one wrong statement about pro forma disclosure. Neither changes a conclusion, but committee use stays restricted. | Medium | Debt documents and combined-business earnings are not supplied, so covenant capacity, guarantors and combined leverage cannot be verified. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| The third quarter interest cover was shown as 7.73x and should read 7.74x. | Coverage remains comfortable; no conclusion changes. | High |

| Earlier notes said no pro forma information existed, but each quarterly report gives pro forma net sales and net income; later notes corrected this. | Combined leverage stays uncomputable because pro forma earnings before interest and depreciation are absent. | High |

| Debt, liquidity and covenant balances trace to the third quarter filing and tie to management's release once 25 of financing costs are allowed for. | Balance sheet inputs for the credit view are reliable. | High |

| The reported covenant ratio of 0.84x reproduces from filed numbers, but the definition is inferred, not read. | Headroom of 4.66x is probably real but unconfirmed without the credit agreement. | Medium |
| Legal documents are not supplied. | Capacity for distributions, priming and the guarantee package cannot be verified. | High |
### Evidence trace view

The credit work for Allison Transmission Holdings Inc is well sourced and committee use is restricted, not blocked. Of the 21 claims traced in the credit driver table below, 19 are verified to a filed page and recompute exactly, 1 is verified with a rounding correction (third quarter interest cover) and 1 is an estimate that rests on stated assumptions (run-rate cash interest). Every derived figure in the financial base, business and transaction and synthesis handoffs was recomputed; the only arithmetic discrepancy is the 7.73x that should be 7.74x. One factual statement in the source readiness and financial base handoffs, that no pro forma disclosure existed, is wrong: each quarterly report has a pro forma note (S2 page:9, S3 page:9, S4 page:9). The business and transaction and synthesis handoffs corrected it, and this review confirms the correction. The earlier handoffs cannot be edited, so readers should use the corrected statement. The restrictions that remain are structural: no executed legal documents, no pro forma earnings before interest and depreciation, an unresolved guarantor roster and preliminary purchase accounting. No source is dated after the 2026-11-05 cutoff, and subsequent events are labelled as such.
### Contrary evidence

The strongest evidence against the synthesis view of a moderate and improving credit is the perimeter mismatch: trailing Adjusted EBITDA holds the acquired unit for three of four quarters, so reported leverage is overstated, yet the acquired unit earns a 12.7% Adjusted EBITDA margin against 37.8% for the legacy unit, so a full year would add less earnings than its sales share suggests (S7 page:10). A second counterpoint is that management's 2.0x net leverage target is below the 2.47x computed on the reported trailing basis, while distributions of 195 over nine months continue. Both would win if the pro forma earnings were weak or if the credit agreement allowed large distributions, which the pack cannot show.
